text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English poet and playwright CHRISTOPHER MARLOWE was born in 1664.
QUEEN ANNE, the last STUART ruler of England, was born on this day in 1665.
Sir HENRY IRVING, English actor was born in 1838; he became the first actor to be knighted.
Legendary American baseball player GEORGE HERMAN (BABE RUTH) was born in 1895.
Former American President RONALD REAGAN was born in 1911.
Hungarian actress ZSA ZSA GABOR was born on this day in 1919.

US singer and actor FABIAN (FABIANO FORTE) was born in 1943. He was discovered by the owner of Chancellor Records company who though the 14-year-old was a cross between ELVIS PRESLEY and RICKY NELSON. FABIAN had most of his hits during PRESLEY's military service. The hits included "Turn Me Loose" (1959), "Tiger" (1959) and "Hound Dog Man" (1959).

US singer and daughter of NAT 'KING' COLE, NATALIE COLE, was born in 1950. Her first album appeared in 1975 and three years later she was named best singer of the year in the United States. Her hits included "I've Got Love On My Mind" (1977), "Pink Cadillac" (1988) and "Miss You Like Crazy" (1989).

British pop singer RICK ASTLEY was born in 1966. He released solo records from 1987 and had hits with "Never Gonna Give You Up" (1987), "When I Fall In Love" (1987), "Together Forever" (1988), "She Wants To Dance With Me" (1988) and "Take Me To Your Heart" (1988).
** EVENTS **
1515 : MANUTIUS ALDUS, the first publisher of paperbacks
and inventor of 'italics', died.
1685 : CHARLES II died after a long illness. Doctors had

tried several remedies, including draining a litre of his blood at a time and daubing his feet with a mixture of resin and pigeon droppings, and he lasted a week of this treatment before passing away.
1804 : The man who discovered Oxygen, English clergyman
JOSEPH PRIESTLEY, died.
1840 : Britain reluctantly annexed New Zealand. 50 Maori
chiefs accepted British sovereignty in a treaty signed by Captain WILLIAM HOBSON at Waitangi.
1865 : ROBERT E. LEE became commander of the Confederate
Armies in America.
1917 : British women over the age of 30 were allowed to
vote.
1926 : Child prodigy YEHUDI MENUHIN made his
violin-playing debut in Paris.
1943 : Actor ERROL FLYNN was cleared of three rape
charges by a Court in Los Angeles.
1952 : King GEORGE VI of Great Britain and Northern
Ireland died and was succeeded by his daughter, ELIZABETH II.
1958 : Seven Manchester United soccer players were killed
when their plane crashed in Munich while returning from a match in Belgrade where they'd just qualified for the European Cup semi-finals.
1961 : A deal was announced for Australian wheat. One
million tons were to be sold to China in the year.
1964 : Britain and France agreed to build a Channel
tunnel costing 160 million pounds.
1976 : In Sydney PATRICIA O'SHANE became the first
Aborigine to be admitted to the bar.
1976 : Maoris welcomed the decision to change the
national day from New Zealand day to Waitangi Day.
1980 : A Flinders University economist Professor BLANDY
suggested that a special tax be levied on all graduates. Was this the birthplace of HECS - the Higher Education Contribution Scheme?
1984 : Five police were sent to trial charged with the

manslaughter of Aboriginal youth JOHN PAT at Roebourne in Western Australia. The police were cleared. JOHN PAT was found dead in the Roebourne police lock-up after a fight between police and Aborigines at a local hotel.
1985 : An Irish freed Australia's most wanted man, ROBERT

TRIMBOLE. He was wanted over the drug-related deaths of crusader DONALD MACKAY in Griffith and couriers DOUGLAS and ISABEL WILSON. A technical hitch with warrants prepared by Australian police allowed TRIMBOLE freedom. Irish police had detained him under the country's anti-terrorist laws to give Australian authorities time to prepare extradition orders.
